IdentityA skill expert and opportunist: locks, traps, scouting and talk, then a vicious strike from behind when the moment comes.

Rogue Progression Table

These values apply from the listed level until the next row. Exploit's dice stay smaller than the Assassin's Sneak Attack because its trigger is easier to meet.

Level by Level at a Glance

What you gain and when. Full details are under Class Abilities.

LvlYou gain
1Thief Skills, Backstab, Exploit (Sneak Attack), Snatch, Precise Strikes, Hide and Move Silently
2Cunning Step, Hit and Run
3Dirty Fighting, Detect Secret/Concealed Doors
4Evasive Manoeuvre
5Cut and Run (Extra Attack), Thief Skills (Master)
6Skill Mastery, Uncanny Dodge
7Evasion
8Sixth Sense
9Exploit 2d6, Dirty Fighting improves, kit improves
13Knight attack track, Precise Strikes improves
15+1 Dexterity
17Fleet Shadow, Exploit 3d6
20Evasive Manoeuvre improves, Renown: Guild House
24Perfect Timing, Unseen Stride

Class Abilities

1st Level

  • Thieves' Cant: the coded slang and signs thieves use to talk in plain sight.
  • Thief Skills: Trained in Lockpicking, Traps, Pick Pocket and Climb (Book II), on top of your 3 starting skills, and Master in all four from 5th level. Your versions are better than anyone else's:
    • Lockpicking: you may try a lock you failed again after 1 minute; the one-attempt-per-level limit doesn't apply to you. From 5th level, you pick a lock in one round.
    • Traps: you disarm a trap in one round, not a minute, and a failure sets it off only on a natural 1. You can re-arm a trap you disarmed, or carry a small one away and set it elsewhere.
    • Pick Pocket: your DC is 10 + half the target's Level, and a failure by less than 5 goes unnoticed.
    • Climb: you roll Dexterity and climb at full speed with a hand free. From 5th level, you can climb sheer walls and overhangs, with Disadvantage.

Backstab

  • Effect: Once per round, when you hit a creature that cannot see you with a light or finesse melee weapon, multiply the weapon's damage dice (double at 1st level, rising to sextuple at 20th: see the Rogue Progression Table).

Exploit (Sneak Attack)

  • Effect: Advantage on the attack roll plus a scaling damage die (1d6 at 1st level, rising to 4d6 at 23rd: see the Rogue Progression Table) against a creature that is flanked, in melee with one of your allies and not with you, Restrained, Prone, or that cannot see you, once per round. Usable at range within 30ft, doesn't require a prior stealth check, can't combine with Backstab.

Snatch

  • Effect: Once per round, when your Exploit hits a creature within 5ft of you, you may take one unsecured item from it (a pouch, potion, scroll or wand) instead of the Exploit's damage die: make a Pick Pocket check against your Pick Pocket DC for it (10 + half its Level), and on a success the item is yours.

Precise Strikes

  • Effect: Your weapon attacks deal +1 damage. This applies to every hit, not only Exploits. Improves to +2 at 6th level, +3 at 9th, +4 at 12th, +6 at 13th, +7 at 14th, +8 at 16th, +9 at 18th, +10 at 20th, +11 at 22nd and +12 at 24th.

Hide and Move Silently

  • Effect: Your pace sets the roll. Half speed or less: Advantage. Normal speed: a normal roll. Running or charging: Disadvantage (where anyone else can't try at all).
  • Together: you may Hide and Move Silently at once, at your pace, with no extra penalty.
  • Lightly obscured: you count as Hidden while lightly obscured even on a result of 12 to 14.
  • Listen: you ignore the Disadvantage for listening through a solid barrier (see Disengage & Hide in The Arneyan Codex), and you follow whispered speech through a door as if you were in the room.

2nd Level

Cunning Step

  • Effect: Once per round, you may move away from a creature in melee reach without provoking opportunity attacks.

Hit and Run

  • Effect: On a turn you make an attack, your speed increases by 10ft (20ft from 13th level). Once per round, you can move through one enemy's space. Moving through that space doesn't provoke Attacks of Opportunity.

3rd Level

Detect Secret/Concealed Doors

  • Effect: Advantage on checks to find secret or concealed doors, plus a free check whenever you pass within 10ft of one.

Dirty Fighting

  • Effect: Advantage on Dirty Trick, Disarm and Trip contests (see Combat Manoeuvres in The Arneyan Codex), and you may use Dexterity for all three.
  • 9th level: once per round, when your Exploit hits, you may make a Dirty Trick, Disarm or Trip contest against that creature as part of the hit

4th Level

Evasive Manoeuvre

  • Effect: The first melee attack against you each round has Disadvantage. It doesn't work while you are surprised.
  • 20th level: the first two melee attacks against you each round have Disadvantage

5th Level

Cut and Run

  • Effect: When you use your action to attack, make one additional weapon attack as part of it, with Disadvantage (see Extra attacks in The Arneyan Codex).
  • Next to an ally: the extra attack has no Disadvantage against a creature next to one of your allies.
  • Slip away: if that attack hits, your movement this turn doesn't provoke Attacks of Opportunity from that creature.
  • Exploit: still applies to only one attack per round.

6th Level

Skill Mastery

  • Effect: Treat any d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10 on Rogue class skills and Thief Skills.

Uncanny Dodge

  • Effect: Once per round, when an attacker you can see hits you, halve the damage.

7th Level

Evasion

  • Effect: When you succeed on a Reflex save against an effect that deals half damage on a success, you take none. If you fail, you take half.

8th Level

  • Sixth Sense: Advantage on checks to avoid being surprised

15th Level

  • Dexterity Bonus: permanent +1 Dexterity. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).

17th Level

  • Fleet Shadow: running or charging no longer gives Disadvantage on Hide or Move Silently, and once per round you may Hide as part of your movement, even while observed, if you end that movement in cover or heavy obscurement.

20th Level

Renown: Guild House

  • Effect: You may found a guild house (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d6 apprentice thieves and a fence join it. While you hold it, you have Advantage on checks to gather information in its city.

24th Level

  • Unseen Stride: Hide and Move Silently have Advantage at any speed, even while running or charging.

Perfect Timing

  • Effect: Once per encounter, act first in the round, whatever initiative says.

Kits: Arneyan Thief Cultures

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Rogue folder. Drag one onto your character.

Each Rogue Kit is built on one thief skill and makes you better still at it, on top of the Rogue's own edge. The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.
